To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the surfactant Glucopon- 425N is an effective agent for recovering DNAPL from sandpacks, that the surfactants effectiveness in removing DNAPL depends on the pore size and flow rate of surfactant, and that the surfactent is effective in removing DNAP from both 30- and 50-mesh sands, but that the effectiveness is greater in the 30- than in the 50- mesh sand.
the presence of macro emulsion in surfactant flushing can lead to higher solubilized PCE recovery and that the presence of residual water in the sandpack can lead to higher recovery of residual PCE.
the presence of macro-emulsion flow is the dominant mechanism of recovery of DNAPL from sandpacks and the surfactant concentration controls the amount of PCE that is solubilized in the macroemulsion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technology to remediate DNAPL contamination in the subsurface.
the evaluation of the effectiveness of surfactant flooding for remediation of DNAPLs in porous media and with the development of an experimental technique for studying the process.
the evaluation of a surfactant system for DNAPL recovery in a water-saturated porous medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the surfactant concentration is the dominant factor in determining the performance of surfactant flooding in the recovery of DNAPL.
surfactant flushing is an effective means of removing DNAPL from the subsurface and can be an effective remediation tool.
the surfactant concentration and the pore-size of the sandpack are the two important variables that control the DNAPL recovery process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
surfactant flushing can be effective in recovering residual PCE from sandpacks.
the surfactant is capable of recovering a large fraction of the DNAPL from a sandpack.
the macroemulsion flow is the dominant mechanism for DNAPL recovery from a water-saturated sand and the surfactant concentration is the key variable for the recovery process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surfactant concentration is the most important factor for DNAPL recovery.
the presence of surfactant in the pore water does not guarantee recovery of all the residual DNAPL and the residual DNAPl is not always recovered as a free phase.
the surfactant flushing process in the presence of DNAPL is a complex process that is influenced by a variety of factors.
